notes.title: We’ve given the Trolls vs Vikings IP to the University College of Kristiania!
notes.notes: [p]Wait, what? Are we crazy? Nope — just excited. For a limited time, Kristiania’s excellent game design students get full access across the Trolls vs Vikings IP: all assets, graphics, animations, UI, music…everything.  Their mission? To build their own student game!  [/p][p][/p][p][b]How it works:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Part of the 3rd semester Game Design Bachelor (Game Production 1). [/p][/*][*][p]4-month project simulating a full game production. [/p][/*][*][p]Phase 1 – Pre-production: Teams of 3 pitch, plan, budget, and design [/p][/*][*][p]Phase 2 – Production: The class unites to build the selected concept in 6 weeks, studio-style. [/p][/*][*][p]Students handle coding, design, sounds, and new assets — Megapop provides the Trolls vs Vikings foundation and spar on the pitches -Students have total creative freedom — any genre, any style.  [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Release:[/b] As a free game on [url="https://itch.io/"]https://itch.io/[/url].  [/p][p][/p][p][b]Context:[/b] Similar projects ran with Funcom’s Conan IP (RAM and Conan the Culinarian on [url="https://itch.io/"]https://itch.io/[/url]).But this is the first time a company has gone all-in, giving students full reign.  [/p][p][/p][p][b]Learning outcomes:[/b] [/p][list][*][p]Working with an IP and a professional studio [/p][/*][*][p]Running a full production cycle [/p][/*][*][p]Pitching, planning, managing deadlines, and shipping a game.  [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Currently: [/b]there are 23 concepts → 16 → turning into 8 shortly. Final pitchround decides the winner heading into production.  [/p][p][/p][p]So, these students are in many ways the future of Norwegian game development. We can’t wait to see their ideas come to life, we are sure they will inspire us back.[/p]

notes.title: Our Trolls and Vikings now speak in Portuguese & Brazilian
notes.notes:
[p][b]Olá![/b][/p][p][/p][p]That might not be my usual greeting, but today it fits just right—we’re launching a major [b]localization update[/b] for [i]Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/i]! We’re now proudly catering to the [b]Lusophone world[/b] with not one, but two new languages: [b]Portuguese (Portugal)[/b] and [b]Brazilian Portuguese[/b]. Brazil in particular is a rising force in global gaming, and Latin America as a whole is exploding with creativity and passion for games—both playing and making them.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="c-1pa1sNBIg;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Having a dedicated [b]Brazilian Portuguese[/b] patch is a first for me personally, and it’s especially meaningful—Brazil is a country I’ve spent a lot of time in, and I really hope to visit again. Huge thanks, Rodolpho![/p][p][/p][p]🎧 Check out his work here: [/p][p][url="https://www.behance.net/rodolphoMorais"]https://www.behance.net/rodolphoMorais[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Next up, we’re working on two more languages—and later this summer, we’ll also update the [i]Steam[/i] page with broader language support.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s it for today! We hope you enjoy this update—and as always, [b]let us know how we’re doing[/b]![/p][p][/p][p][b]Best wishes,

notes.title: "Moving on Up" update is now live for Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn
notes.notes:
[p]Finally, the new content patch [i]“Moving on Up”[/i] goes live! We’re also introducing our [b]very first live sale[/b] on the project—so for those of you on the fence, this might be a great opportunity to grab the game at a discount.[/p][p][/p][p]The patch then took a little longer than planned… Sorry about that! My whole family and I went down with a nasty variant of Covid, so the last two weeks were pretty much spent in bed. No fun![/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, the team’s been busy—and as you may have seen, we even announced and launched the [b]demo of our upcoming city-builder game, Life Below[/b], last week. Exciting times for us in Megapop, but like I mentioned in the last update, we’re fully committed to keeping new content flowing into [i]Trolls Reborn[/i]![/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="8LaOI63vbNc;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]SO, WHAT IS THIS PATCH ALL ABOUT?[/b][/p][p][/p][p]First of all, there’s a brand-new area: [b]The Magic Forest[/b]![/p][p]I think Mikael Noguchi (Art Director on [i]Trolls[/i]) did a fantastic job creating something ethereal and otherworldly. It’s colourful and sizzling—very much in line with the Trolls aesthetic. Hope you’ll like it! (We’ve already drawn two more playfield backgrounds coming up in future patches!)[/p][p][/p][p][b]NOW, ONTO GAMEPLAY:[/b][/p][p][/p][p]This patch adds [b]five new levels[/b], each one ramping up the challenge. They’re all centered around something uniquely [i]Trolls[/i]: [b]moving units[/b] (hence the name “Moving on Up”).[/p][p][/p][p]I’ve wanted to create more levels based around this gameplay type for a long time. Now we’ve done it—so please let us know what you think![/p][p][/p][p]The setup is that a small band of Trolls is on the move through the magical forest. Each level gives you a specific loadout of movable units. Thor and I worked to make sure each level builds on the last—you’ll see some units rotate in and out, and the Moonstone and Spell loadouts shift a bit from level to level. There’s an intended sense of progression and escalating complexity—and hopefully, they’re all fun to play![/p][p][/p][p]Fingar also added support for [b]setting spell amounts per level[/b], overriding player setups. Honestly, I’m not sure why we didn’t do this earlier—it gives us much more control to fine-tune specific challenges. You’ll see how it works in the new special mission![/p][p][/p][p]As for difficulty... well, that depends on your skills.[/p][p][/p][p]I promised to go overboard with the complexity, and I think we delivered. On the fifth and final level, we tested some borderline impossible setups. I personally tried one variant like 15 times before admitting: “Okay... this is impossible.” So, we nerfed it slightly and added a couple more spells—because when something is [i]too[/i] hard, it stops being fun. Now the final level should still be brutal—but beatable (for the best of you!).[/p][p][/p][p]Personally, I can blitz through the first three levels on double speed, but once I hit level 4 and 5, I really need to slow down and think things through. Now we look forward to hearing how [i]you[/i] experience them—that’ll help us fine-tune future balancing.[/p][p][/p][p]The goal here is to push for [b]super-active, super-tactical gameplay[/b], where you’re constantly moving units around and coordinating them tightly. I don’t know any other tower defense game that leans into this the way [i]Trolls[/i] does, so it felt great to double down on what makes us uniquely us.[/p][p][/p][p][b]BEYOND CONTENT: BUGS, POLISH AND UPGRADES[/b][/p][p][/p][p]The extra time while I was out did lead to some positives—Fingar (our lead coder) managed to squash a ton of bugs and clean up some long-standing issues.[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s the list:[/p][p]
• Improved upscaling for a bunch of UI sprites
• Fixed issue where Mudwrestling achievement wouldn’t unlock
• Various localization fixes
• Spells can now be set per level (overriding player setups)
• UI layout fixes to support more languages
• Updated card graphics
• Updated level preview UI (default levels and Valhalla)
• Improved low-res graphics in the world map
• Added safety checks for Loki-scripted event in Eric boss fight
• Old star graphics now hidden
• Improved button highlights (main menu, world map, panels)
• Returning from a side quest now takes you back to the side quest menu (instead of world map)
• Updated art for world map’s Rune Totem buttons
• Units in victory screen now sorted by class (boss on top)
• Chinese, Taiwanese, and Portuguese localizations added (going live in next patches; currently in testing)[/p][p][/p][p]There are more tweaks and fixes in the backlog—and as always, if you spot something we’ve missed, let us know and we’ll look into it![/p][p][/p][p][b]THAT'S IT FOR NOW![/b][/p][p][/p][p]As a summary I’m really happy with how these new levels turned out, and had a [b]LOT[/b] of fun playing and tweaking them together with Thor (gameplay designer on [i]Trolls Reborn[/i]). I’m obviously biased—but I really hope you’ll enjoy them as much as we do.[/p][p][/p][p]Now it’s up to you to judge.[/p][p][/p][p]As for what’s next—we’re already working on the next patch. Much of the base content is ready, but it’ll take a few weeks before it hits testing.[/p][p][/p][p]Let us know how we’re doing—so we can keep making [i]Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/i] better for y’all.[/p][p][/p][p]All the best,
[b]Jørgen Tharaldsen[/b]
[i]Game Director, Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/i][/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: Game Director Update: 'Moving on up' content patch coming soon
notes.notes:
Heya fine people, hope life is treating you well. 

It’s been a super busy period for us here at Megapop, with moving the company to shiny new offices, and developing a Steam demo on our upcoming city-builder ‘Life Below’ being key culprits.  Both have been long in the coming, so good to get progress there. Thankfully, there is always something going on, and indeed so it is within Trolls Reborn. 

As far as new content we already know the next patch is called “Moving on up”. We have the first three levels done and tested now,  and aim to make two more levels next week.  As per player input one will be a very challenging one, he he, with the balance mantra being “if we can do it, so can you”. Look forward to feedback on that one! 

https://www.youtube.com/embed/QJS9nHDuxGk

In this update we are playing around with a limited amount of units, with Buster and the Dwarf being the two main players. They work really well in tandem when played right, and that is exactly what this string of missions asks you to do. You need to work all across the battlefield, while considering move times, heal times, reach of that dwarven chain, and so on. Personally I often find the levels with movable units some of the most fun we have. Now have emphasized that, and removed the general riff raff that happens to moving units when there are many ranged Trolls. It should be fun! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/332f7555d275e29d5281f65e2d016832d48c55da.jpg[/img]
 
We heard here and there we should add more visual variety to the game, so for this patch we are adding a brand new background we call “magical forest”. Since this special mission is focused around the movable Trolls, I know Thor (the game designer) is looking into lore about being lost in the woods in a far away strange forest filled with mushrooms…fighting Vikings looking for gold (ah, some things never change, do they). We have then already drawn up three new backgrounds that we aim to launch over the next few updates, with Magical Forest going first.  

There has been a stated wish to add more Trolls and Vikings, and Spells, and we, too, want to do that. We have a list of candidates we have right now, but before making promises we rather want to flesh out some more details before we share. As a teaser we got AD Mikael to draw a new spell suggestion (based on player feedback) where the idea is that this spell can torpedo the holes Vikings are jumping up from. Bunker-Buster, indeed. Not usable for all levels, it could prove truly helpful in both later Valhalla levels and levels with many holes. So a very specific yet highly effective use. Still design to be done on that one, but a fun art piece to share!   
 
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/363c0d29073a78b30a5af1cd45b71e8fa1bffd46.jpg[/img]
 (a Troll bunker-buster – have a cigar!) 

There are then also some bugs we have on our list that will be squashed, will update on that as the list goes final. 

When it comes to Trolls Reborn ahead, we just had a Megapop strategy day in Stockholm. There we went through our goals and plans until 2035 (so then our dreams, too!). We agreed to keep on supporting Trolls into 2026 with fresh updates, hopefully learning as much as possible on running a game on Steam, and rather take stock next year. In addition to our upcoming city-builder, we agreed to keep on making strategy-type games for Steam (like Trolls is) into the future,  so ‘hybdrid TD’ is then the name of the game. More on that…much later.  

That’s it for today. For those of you who chose to read these updates, play our games and support us, I simply wanted you to know that you mean a lot to us. In return we promise to give back as good as we can! 

The new content patch is now around two weeks out, so will update you on that as it gets close!   

Thanks for playing.

[b]All the best,
Jørgen Tharaldsen, Game Director, Trolls Reborn [/b]

notes.title: 'Moonstone Madness' Update now available!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, hope you're all hanging in there during these wild times. It seems Loki's up to his old tricks, tempting folks to chase after gold without thinking of the fallout.​

Fittingly, our first content patch, [b]Moonstone Madness[/b], dives into the theme of taking risks for greater rewards. When we first dreamed it up months ago, it felt like a fun concept. Now, it mirrors the world around us more than we ever expected.​

A few weeks into our launch, and things are looking up. We've gathered more than 50 reviews from players and curators—many of them glowing! It's fantastic to see that those who've joined us on this journey are loving the game. A massive thank you for playing and for taking the time to share your thoughts!​

We've also spotted many streamers diving into the game. Watching skilled players tackle [u]Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/u] has been both entertaining and enlightening. While we might not catch every stream, we're taking notes and learning heaps as we move forward.​

Sure, our numbers are very modest compared to the big hitters, but [u]Trolls[/u] is a labor of love. We're here for the long haul, committed to bringing you updates and new content.​

[h2]Now, let’s dive into Moonstone Madness, our first content patch[/h2]

From the title, you see that this special mission centers around Moonstone, and pre-placed Hacks in the levels. As the difficulty ramps up, these Hacks are forced closer to the frontlines, emphasizing that classic risk/reward balance.​
[list]
 	[*][b]Early Levels:[/b] The first two are relatively forgiving, with four Hacks positioned mid-field.​[/*]
 	[*][b]Cranking Up the Heat:[/b] By level 3 and 4, things get intense. I've played through various setups and found number 4 particularly challenging, with a personal success rate hovering around 40%. But with some trial and error, effective strategies do emerge.​[/*]
 	[*][b]The Final Showdown:[/b] The last level is a wild ride. We've nudged the Hacks back a row due to the chaos, but losing any of them isn't an option! A top-tier spell and shard setup will be your best friends here.​[/*]
[/list]
Things get especially hairy when the Ram-bock minibosses charge in, hurling some of the fiercest Vikings straight at your Hacks. You'll need to have your spells ready and possibly some Zaps on hand off cool-down. Taking out those Vikings before they strike your Hacks is crucial. This mission can and will end brutally swiftly if your strategy isn't on point.​

Our game designer, Thor (not the god, though he's pretty mighty in his own right), has woven a little story into the final level of this campaign. We're still gauging how much narrative to infuse into [u]Trolls[/u], but we enjoy crafting these tales, and we hope they add a touch of flair.​

[previewyoutube=WM1ateDQdkY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What's Else is Brewing:[/h2]
[list]
 	[*][b]Bug Fixes:[/b] We've squashed several bugs and will roll out a detailed list when the patch drops.​ This includes some localization fixes and making the 'Kill Thor before his goats' achievement work again.[/*]
 	[*][b]Achievement Tweak:[/b] Based on feedback, notably from 先辈 dvN_ 🦋, we've adjusted the "War Without End" achievement. Instead of requiring 100,000 Viking defeats, we've dialed it down to 25,000. Still a hefty challenge, but more attainable.​[/*]
 	[*][b]Shard Rewards Streamlined:[/b] Now, diving straight into harder levels will also unlock the shards from the easier ones. If you've got the skills, there's no need to grind through the easy stuff.​ Another player’s feedback thing, keep ‘em coming as this obviously makes the game better (and we missed out on it).[/*]
 	[*][b]Localization Efforts:[/b] We're kicking off a Portuguese translation, with a Brazilian freelancer on the job. Look out for this in our next content patch, aptly named "Moving on Up." We're also eyeing Korean and Chinese translations to welcome more players into our community, but this may take us longer to achieve. Regardless we shall add more languages to the Steam page itself, but we want to work a bit on a new text before those come. Tinker tinker![/*]
 	[*][b]Visual Variety:[/b] We're exploring new backgrounds and considering adding more Trolls and Vikings to the mix. That said, for the next few updates, our focus will be on special missions, languages, quality of life improvements, and addressing your feedback (and those pesky bugs).​ And probably a couple of new backgrounds.[/*]
[/list]
That's the scoop for today. The patch is slated to launch late next week. We'd love to hear your thoughts on "Moonstone Madness" once you've had a chance to dive in. Your feedback is invaluable as we continue to evolve the game

All the best,

[b]Jørgen and Team Trolls Reborn[/b]

notes.title: How the Vikings were created
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

I’m currently playing through the five new levels in our first content patch—things are coming together nicely, and I hope you'll enjoy them! We had a great production meeting today about how to deliver Trolls updates throughout 2025. More on that content in a few days.

Today, I wanted to take a detour and share a little mini-update around a “speed painting” by Mikael Noguchi, our amazing Art Director on Trolls vs Vikings. Just for fun—so you can see how he created the new Vikings using Procreate, and maybe get to know Mikael and our art philosophy a bit better.

Some background: Mikael was part of the original Trolls vs Vikings team, and nearly all the art you see in Reborn comes from his imagination, refined together with the team. Mikael has drawn all his life, earning a solid reputation as a street artist, and he has an almost obsessive joy in creating.

Case in point: anytime a meeting ends, there will be drawings. Often many. Two weeks ago, I left a contract with signatures on my desk near the office couch. The next day, it had doodles all over it—he just saw paper he could draw on. Fair game, right?

Mikael began his game career over 30 years ago at Funcom, before co-founding Innerloop (Project IGI) and Artplant (Battlestar Galactica Online, Game of Thrones Online). Some of you may remember classics like Project IGI, Joint Strike Fighter, Anarchy Online, The Longest Journey, Fatal Fury, Samurai Shodown, and many more where Mikael’s art played a key role. For the past 13 years, we’ve been lucky to work together at Megapop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/355d44a984a7a216c17615f16cb9d14d249050ec.jpg[/img]

While Mikael is our go-to AD for 2D games like Trolls, we’re often hired to do creative work for others too. You’ll find Mikael’s and Megapop’s art across other games, newspapers, books, magazines, murals, portraits (he was just on a big Norwegian TV show for this), TV shows, and commercials. We’ve worked with pop artists like Alan Walker, A Tribe Called Quest, girl in red—even Justin Bieber. In fact, that’s part of Mikael’s work this week, and we can’t wait to show it off. It’s a privilege to help others create.

When it comes to the art in Trolls, it’s built around Mikael’s distinct comic-book style. We aimed for something vibrant, timeless, and fun—art that isn’t tied to a specific era but has a strong visual identity. Something that could “live forever.” At the same time, we wanted to bring myths and folklore into the game in a way that felt authentic, while giving our Trolls real heart and personality.

And of course—we wanted it to be fun to look at and play.

People often praise the game’s vibe and charm, though some wish we’d gone for a darker look. Maybe we should have, maybe not. For all the coziness, there’s plenty of brutal action too :D

When creating new art for a 2D-style game like Trolls, we usually have gameplay already locked in, and then go straight into production. For Reborn, I really wanted to redo the old Viking models and reanimate them (wrote about this in a previous update), and Mikael agreed. The original Vikings were among the first things he created at Megapop back in 2012, so it was time for an upgrade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/ed23ac99bda4ba1b2315a0bfbd69516186fad0fb.jpg[/img]

Since Reborn is a reimagining rather than a brand-new game, we aimed to “make it fit” within the existing structure—sizes, areas, and technical constraints. We were adding a ton of new content, so we had to pick our development battles wisely. Rescaling everything would’ve meant a massive effort in recalibrating hitboxes, positions, animations—you name it.

So, Mikael started with the old Viking model and drew “on shape” using Procreate—his go-to tool for sketching and concept work. Staying creative within those constraints was key.

As we explored directions—colors, beards, weapons, animations, how they look when hit or dying—Mikael quickly developed a strong vision for how the Viking would feel in-game.

It only took about a day to land on something we liked (see the video!), followed by a few more days of testing and iteration. We compared it to the old version, checked how it looked on backgrounds, stacked multiples together to see how they blended, tested silhouettes—basically: “How does this unit feel when played?”

[previewyoutube=smAMB5UAuEY;full][/previewyoutube]

Once the visual was approved, Mikael “chopped” the Viking into parts—arms, legs, head, alternate heads for damage states, etc.—so our animator Aslak could start bringing it to life. That kicked off another process of micro-adjustments—maybe a beard needed shifting, or a cloth piece moved differently in animation. Test, test, test—and then voila, it’s in-game.

This is a very non-technical explanation (happy to go deeper if you’d like!), but the essence is: we build fast, visually, and hands-on. For Trolls—and for Mikael—that works beautifully. Hope you agree!

That’s it for today. Tonight, I’m diving back into testing the next Trolls update. Give us a couple of weeks and we’ll have it in your hands—plus a few extra changes.

As always, hit us up with any questions or thoughts!

All the best,

[b]Jørgen, Game Director
Trolls vs Vikings Reborn [/b]

notes.title: Bug Fixes & Improvements Update #01
notes.notes:
[b]🎉 First Post-Launch Patch![/b]
Hey everyone! Whey! It’s time for our first update after launch. This one’s all about fixing bugs and improving screen and localization issues. Instead of waiting to roll these into a bigger content patch, we decided to swing them out quickly.

Here’s what’s included:

[b]🔤 Localization & UI[/b]
[list]
 	[*]A systemic localization update based on reports from Spanish-speaking players.
Some UI screens didn’t display the proper text or language version—this should now be resolved.
Bonus: This fix improves the experience for all other non-English languages too.[/*]
 	[*][b]“Normal mode” has been renamed to “Easy”[/b]
[list]
 	[*]This better reflects the actual difficulty of that mode. Nevermind that we are a game that goes straight from easy to hard, but…we can live with that.[/*]
 	[*]Most of our work on [u]Trolls Reborn[/u] has gone into [b]Hard[/b] and [b]Brutal[/b], where the true juicy challenge lies. This name change is a quick clarity tweak more than anything.[/*]
 	[*]And yes—future updates will definitely include proper Easy content (because variety matters), but our design hearts beat hardest for the core-gamer modes.[/*]
[/list]
[/*] 	[*]The [b]Preview Panel[/b] now correctly displays [b]localized labels[/b] on the difficulty buttons.[/*]

[/*]

We’re already working on our next content patch, which will include:
[list]

 	[*]Balance improvements for [b]shard execution[/b][/*]
 	[*]We now have a bunch of [b]community-suggested features and tweaks[/b] (and a few surprises from our own dark trollish minds). We definitively value these a lot. We can’t promise we can make all of it, but they are absolutely part of the mix. Keep em coming, please![/*]
[/list]
If you find bugs, have suggestions, or just want to shout lovingly at us, we’re listening. In the meantime, have fun with Trolls Rebon

All the best,
[b]Jørgen & Team Trolls[/b]

notes.title: Trolls, Gather Round!
notes.notes:
Whey! [u]Trolls vs Vikings Reborn[/u] is now out, and we’re moving into the post-launch period. We plan to keep updating the game as we move forward and hope you’ll join us on that journey.

[h2][b]The First Week – A Wild Ride[/b][/h2]

It’s been an eventful week (it’s never quiet at an indie games studio!). We’ve been closely following the general chatter, reviews, and feedback around the game while running ads, sending out keys to curators, influencers, and press, and generally doing PR while trying to understand what’s been working—and what hasn’t—during this first week of [u]Reborn.[/u]

On the positive side, we got some really strong feedback, and some of it has been genuinely encouraging to read (we made a video with some of the curator quotes—check it out!). True, we didn’t get a lot of sales (we’re in the [u]hundreds[/u] of players, not [u]thousands[/u], so a looong way to go), but… baby steps. As a game developer, you always dream of big numbers, but reality is often different.

Still, our key goal with [u]Reborn[/u] was to make a strong [u]premium[/u] version of the game while pushing it into a much more [u]hardcore gamer[/u] vein. I think we succeeded with our own quality goals—but commercially, we’ve fallen short. As expected, but not as [u]wanted.[/u]

[h2][b]Why This Matters[/b][/h2]

A key motivation for us has been learning how to properly run a game on Steam—keeping it updated, working with players, and supporting it through thick and thin. Personally, I’ve worked on a lot of games over the years, and it’s often about the [u]long[/u] haul when you have great core mechanics.

One of them, [u]Anarchy Online[/u], I worked on for [b]11 years[/b]—and it’s still doing well as it turns [b]24[/b] this year. [u]Trolls[/u] is now [b]11[/b], and hey, wouldn’t it be fun if we made a [b]20-year anniversary[/b] for it one day? We’ll see. But what we [u]do[/u] know is that we plan to support it moving forward!

That said, it’s not [u]all[/u] sunshine and rainbows—we’re standing in the rainy part of the valley, watching those. 😆

[h2][b]What Needs Fixing?[/b][/h2]

 	[h3][*][b] 1 Bugs.[/b][/*][/h3]

We haven’t really seen game-breaking bugs so far—nothing stopping you from playing. And, well… some things reported are even working as intended (the classic [u]“it’s not a bug, it’s a feature”[/u] he he).

That said, we [u]have[/u] found and are fixing a few things—primarily localization issues, where we simply weren’t sharp enough in testing every language to bits. Thanks for pointing those out! We’ve also had a report on an achievement not triggering, so we’re looking into that. A few more things popped up during the week that we’re also checking.

All in all, we haven’t come across any “blocker” bugs—meaning stuff that completely stops you from playing. But there are more of [u]you[/u] than [u]us[/u], so if you [b]do[/b] come across something weird, let us know so we can fix it for the next player!

[h3]
[*]2 Game Balance.
[/h3]

Every morning and afternoon, I bike [b]11 km[/b] along the Oslo fjord to and from work. I listen to music, watch the scenery, and think about game balance. And, well, let’s talk about it.

Right now, most players seem to be judging the game based on [b]Normal mode[/b]—and the general feedback is:

✔ [u]Too easy.[/u]
✔ [u]Too similar to a certain plant-based game (much due to that, too).[/u]

Why is that? Well, the truth is that [b]Normal doesn’t really fight back.[/b] You don’t need to hunker down in deep strategy, manage resources carefully, or react on the fly—it mostly kind of just [u]breezes[/u]. Is that even a problem? Well, where we’ve really [b]pushed[/b] to make [u]Trolls[/u] unique is in its strategic and action gameplay. But if Normal doesn’t [u]ask[/u] you to engage on a “fight for your life” level, many players never experience that depth. That’s what makes this tricky—it’s not a visual thing, it’s a [u]player experience[/u] thing.

During development, we discussed calling [b]Normal mode “Easy”[/b] since the new upgrade system and added spells made it easier than before. Looking at the feedback, we’re seriously considering:

✅ 1) [b]Raising the difficulty of Normal[/b] so that players actually experience what [u]Trolls[/u] is about.
✅ 2) [b]Adding a fourth difficulty[/b] – Normal becomes Easy and a new Normal is made (less likely)

For the record, Hard and [b]Brutal mode[/b] has gotten a lot of solid feedback, so that’s working as intended!

[olist]
 [h2]	[*][b] Requests & Wishlist.[/b][/*][/h2]
[/olist]
We’ve seen quite a few requests for [b]more mini-games.[/b] Our philosophy has been to build [b]special challenges[/b] as part of [u]special missions[/u] rather than casual, side mini-games. But we hear you.

If we were to expand on this, it wouldn’t just be for the sake of adding "more"—it would need to really fit within the game and enhance the experience. Right now, our focus is still on [b]special missions,[/b] but we’re keeping this on our radar. If we see traction, more engagement, and more people joining the [u]Trolls[/u] community, this is something we’d love to explore further.

[h2][b]What’s Next?[/b][/h2]

We’re already diving into our [b]first post-launch update[/b], which will include:

🔥 [b]Bug fixes & polish[/b] – localization fixes, achievement issues, and more.
🔥 [b]Rebalancing[/b]– tweaking Normal mode (or renaming it [u]Easy[/u]?) to better reflect the game.
🔥 [b]New content update[/b] – a [b]brand-new special mission[/b], coming soon!

Beyond that? More balancing, more content, and continued support to push [u]Reborn[/u] to a wider audience.

So let us know what you think! Your feedback helps us shape the game, and we’re here to keep improving.

[b]All the best,[/b]
Jørgen Tharaldsen
Game Director, [u]Trolls vs Vikings[/u]

notes.title: Revamping Viking animations for Reborn
notes.notes:
We wanted to give some shine to the various people working on Trolls vs Vikings Reborn. We have already told you a bit about the music (Aleksandar), and today about the new animations we put into the game. We made all new Vikings models for Reborn, and naturally then made all new Vikings animations to give them more oomph and “weight”.

For this we knew of no better animator than [b]Aslak Helgensen[/b], from [b]Rain Games[/b], who we hired as a freelancer on Trolls Reborn. Last year Aslak was incredibly enough [b]nominated for the Annie Awards[/b] for his animation work on Teslagrad 2. This is the most prestigious award to recognizing excellence in animation across film, television, and video games, so we know Aslak is a top-shelf animator. The new animation then comes on top of the original animation by [b]Voja Dimitrijevic[/b], which we also feel is excellent. Hopefully these two top notch animators make you feel like the Trolls and Vikings come alive within the game. 

And do check out the Rain game titles that Aslak is so involved in, including Teslagrad 1 and 2, they are great!

We then got some words from Aslak, so we leave the rest up to him, with some clips from his work:

[h1]I got a chance to work on the Trolls vs Viking: Reborn![/h1]

The Megapop game series is well known here in Norway so I was excited to get to animate the Viking character. The team is also a super friendly bunch that I enjoyed working with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/97e1a6ad4495392df0a7f2eb711b4ec8fef2c946.gif[/img]

The original games chunky and stompy charm is appealing, and the new designs that were made for the re-release add some nice opportunities for expressive animation. I rummaged a bit for how to make something that feels like the original and is still a clear upgrade. I looked at what the limitations of the original were: Only the necessary moving parts plus little in the way of secondary motion, and concluded that adding overlapping action to more of the costume would be a likely path to success.

My main animation tool for a long time has been Blender so I rigged and animated the character with that tool. It has gotten better support for doing 2D characters, but could use some improvements for Unity support for those features! I added extra controls for such things as the beard and cape and got to work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/a2e0839fc989c3b377c0cf23cdd1ee28b9badec6.gif[/img]

Having access to the original animations made timing easy, but to make actions like attacks more impactful, I added more variation to the easing and bouncy movements to the clothes and beard.  I also took the opportunity to make the death and rise from death animations overly dramatic and silly. I think most animators enjoy some good slapstick and I’m no exception.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45378884/46ab2fccee1204805ab9cd1f8db3bac53f758b4e.gif[/img]

The final result feels like a solid upgrade to me, but also fits right in with the original ensemble of characters. I also had a lot of fun working with this grumpy guy, and I hope you all have fun giving him a good thwacking!

[b]Aslak Helgensen[/b]

notes.title: Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn is Live!
notes.notes:
Finally, the day is here. The day when [b]we finally unleash Trolls vs Vikings[/b] as a premium experience to y’all. To me personally it’s a bit of a dream come true, as the game is now, finally, made with a vision and complexity worthy of a hardcore gamer. Or, so we like to believe.

Over these last few weeks, we have been able to test the game in two demos weeks at Steam, and thankfully it seems well polished, stable and with an, ahem, appropriate difficulty curve. We got a lot of really nice feedback too, so hopefully that helps to get even more players enjoying it. 

[previewyoutube=ZPjSDKAdgX8;full][/previewyoutube]

We have already lined up the three first patches for the game, and beyond that we promise to listen for any ideas, tweaks or updates you feel would make the game even better. 

As you may understand the entire game is a tribute to our Norse and Norwegian heritage, our wild mythology and not the least the weird humour within it. As Norwegians, we grew up with tales of trolls, fierce Viking warriors, strange gods and epic battles. Indeed, some of us on the dev team lives in the Vik region (Vik-ing, is what you call that in Norwegian). So, this feels a bit like home, however weird home is!  

That we now get to bring that to the world, and mix it with some fine-tuned strategy gameplay, is in our very own way a little tribute. On such a day I would also like to thank the fine devs here at Megapop who have poured their hearts into it, as well as NFI who supported us with funds to see the light shine on Midgard once again. And, not the least, all of you players who tested it during the demo weeks. 

Oh, I almost forgot, Loki convinced us to have a special 15% launch sale, so for the first week of sales it dips a divinely 15% below the 5,99 SRP.  Beyond that sale, we feel the price is hopefully a good one. It’s kinda hard to really set these things when you’re an indie developer like us, but there should be tons of content for that price.  

And now, let’s end this with an actual quote from Odin in Havamal. "Better to fight and fall than to live without hope." 

Indeed…Have fun fighting!

Jørgen Tharaldsen
[b]Game Director
Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn [/b]

notes.title: Brutalism – When Trolls Get Serious!
notes.notes:
I don’t want to sound like an [b]elitist[/b]—because that’s not the point. [b]The reason Brutal Mode exists isn’t just to make the game hard.[/b] It’s about [b]respecting players who love deep, tactical gameplay[/b].

For me, games are at their absolute [b]best[/b] when they pull you into a [b]flow state[/b]—that moment when your [b]mind fully locks in[/b], when every move is [b]instinctive[/b], when the [b]outside world disappears[/b] and you’re just [u]there[/u], fully engaged.

That’s what [u]Brutal Mode[/u] is designed for. Not stress. Not frustration. [b]Discovery. Mastery.[/b] That moment when you [b]crack a level that once seemed impossible[/b]—when you analyze, adapt, and suddenly everything clicks. That’s the magic of deep strategy games.

It might sound absurd talking about “zen moments” in a game where Trolls [b]punch Vikings in the face[/b], but that’s exactly what I’m talking about. When you’re in the zone, the [b]graphics, the setting, the art style—it all fades away[/b]. What’s left is just [b]you, your strategy, and the thrill of solving the puzzle.[/b]

Trolls is a really cozy looking game, and in some respect it is “too nice” for its tactical depth. We many times debated [b]going full dark-doom Troll[/b] art style at one point, but in the end, Mikael Noguchi found a style we really liked that spoke across cultures and ages. Still, [b]the depth of the gameplay remained core. As it always should with a Megapop game. [/b]

[b]Your Thoughts? [/b]

We’re def keeping an eye on things, and soon we even launch the entire game. If some levels prove [b]truly impossible[/b] ([u]they aren’t, by the way, so we hope players crack them, git gud style[/u]), we WILL consider some balance tweaks, or maybe drop a strategy video with a couple ways of beating them.

Either way—let us know how we fare so we can optimize the game the best way we can for y‘all.

[b]All the best,[/b]
[b]Jørgen Tharaldsen[/b]
Game Director, [u]Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/u]

notes.title: A Bit of Spiritual Practice for Y’all – The Shaman’s Path
notes.notes:
One of the special missions we’re excited for you to try during Steam Next Fest is [b]The Shaman’s Path[/b]! It highlights the active Shaman units in the game while bringing a mix of tactical choices—you can go full healing, full attack, or anything in between.

The original version of this mission popped up around 2015, focusing on beginner-level gameplay. Not so in the [b]Reborn[/b] edition! We’ve cranked up the challenge with two more complex versions. (At least we [u]think[/u] they're tough—we’ve played so much we might be a little blind to what’s actually difficult.)

This string of five missions revolves around [b]Zap[/b] and [b]Doc[/b], two brothers who chose the Shaman path—calling on ancient Troll gods to channel power onto the battlefield.

[b]Zap[/b] draws from the same lightning pool as Thor (the god, not our game designer Thor). He calls down lightning strikes but needs a bit of spiritual recharge time afterward. Timing those recharges is key—especially when support units vanish in harder levels!

[b]Doc[/b], on the other hand, followed his mother’s dream of him becoming a healer (moms, right?). His specialty? [b]AOE healing[/b] through totems that keep your rocks and brutes alive (or anything else, for that matter). But at [b]Brutal[/b] difficulty, no Trolls will block Vikings for you. You’ll need to heal yourself if you want to deal enough staff damage. Tricky? Yes. Fun? [u]Absolutely[/u] (we hope)!
In this mission, we’ve also removed [b]Hack the resource miner[/b] and spells, focusing entirely on unit-based tactics. Raw gameplay, no fluff. I love these types of missions myself, and hope you will enjoy them too!

[previewyoutube=1wUgnqL7VnE;full][/previewyoutube]

With our launch on [b]March 7th[/b], even more special missions are coming, and we plan to keep rolling them out in batches post-launch. Got ideas for special missions? [b]Let us know![/b] Maybe your idea will be the next one we create!

[b]All the best,[/b]

notes.title: The inspiration for Trolls vs Vikings
notes.notes:
Today I wanted to talk a bit about the background for [u]Trolls Reborn[/u], how it came to be, and what inspired us during development. This is also a bit of a personal journey, but as it's my baby, it makes sense to weave that in.

Ever since we first showed [u]Trolls vs Vikings[/u] at [b]GDC 2013[/b] in California, there has been a lot of interest in the game. Development started in [b]August 2012[/b]. On first sight, [u]Trolls[/u] may remind players of a certain plants-based game—a fact we've never tried to hide. It's definitively a [b]lane defense RTS / tower defense game[/b] with a grid, featuring two opposing forces in a comical style: [b]Trolls vs. Vikings and their gods[/b]. That said, let’s explore what makes [u]Trolls[/u] uniquely itself.

[h2][b]A Lifelong Journey in Games[/b][/h2]

My personal background in the games industry spans [b]32 years[/b]. I first got into games at [b]five years old[/b], when a neighbor got an Atari with Pong. From that moment, I was hooked, playing everything I could get my hands on. By [b]12 years old[/b], I decided I wanted to work with games, and at [b]19 years old[/b], I did exactly that. Something rather unheard of in Norway at that time, so it was not a life choice I got a lot of support for. Still, ever since 5 years old I’ve then tried to play games almost every day— and still do. To me, games IS my life.

One of the benefits of being old and loving all forms of games is that I’ve seen nearly [b]every new genre emerge[/b] as it happened. I’ve always been fascinated by innovation and how new ways of making games evolve. At [b]Funcom[/b], we introduced many innovations to the MMORPG genre, which I worked on for a long time.

The [b]tower defense genre[/b] was something I picked up as it emerged. The early days beyond the mods, when it reached the mass market, saw [b]Bloons (2007), Gemcraft 2008), and Desktop Tower Defense (2007)[/b] as browser-based hits. With the iPhone in [b]2008[/b], TD games transitioned from browser to [b]mobile[/b] and [b]PC installs[/b], with games like [b]Fieldrunners (2008), Plants vs. Zombies (2009), Kingdom Rush (2011), and Sanctum (2011)[/b].

[h2][b]Key Inspirations[/b][/h2]

Games like [b]PvZ[/b] and [b]Sanctum[/b] were major eye-openers for me. I loved how [b]Sanctum[/b] incorporated active gameplay elements—something I felt many TD games were missing, and how plants was so well balanced. I played [b]these TD games to death[/b], often pushing them to their limits. In [b]Bloons[/b], my PC would crash from too many enemies on screen. In [b]PvZ[/b], I was obsessed with competing on the [b]global leaderboards[/b], breaking the game down [b]to the pixel level[/b] for optimization.

At the time, I worked at [b]Funcom[/b], where making a strategy game wasn't on the agenda. But [b]ideas started to form[/b]…

[h2][b]The Birth of Trolls vs Vikings[/b][/h2]

Out of all the TD games, we saw [b]the grid-lane layout[/b] in [u]Plants vs. Zombies[/u] as the [b]most expandable[/b]. When we launched [b]Megapop[/b], we wanted to take the genre further. We looked at elements from [b]Sanctum, Street Fighter, tactics games like Final Fantasy, and even Castle Fights from Heroes III[/b].

It started with the Shaman [u]Zap[/u] and his active lightning strike. Then [b]Mikael Noguchi[/b] (who had worked on [b]Fatal Fury and Samurai Showdown[/b] ports) designed [u]Buster[/u], but as a static melee tank. He was inspired by [b]Guile from Street Fighter[/b]. Our [b]lead coder Christian[/b] then for fun implemented him as a [b]mobile unit[/b]. And from there on it kinda grew. The result? A [b]lane defense game where characters moved around[/b]—something that felt fresh and fun.

Our [b]lead designer Thomas[/b] later added [b]healing mechanics to Buster[/b], and we added more [b]active[/b] units like the [b]Dwarf[/b] and the [b]Shaman healer[/b]. However, we had to [b]strike a balance[/b]—it was becoming too [b]action-focused[/b], so we refined the gameplay while keeping it engaging and active.

[h2][b]Standing on the Shoulders of Giants[/b][/h2]

When we started development, we didn’t even know [u]Plants vs. Zombies 2[/u] was coming. Since PvZ1 had stopped development, we felt it was the [b]perfect time[/b] to evolve the genre. Just as [b]RTS, FPS, MMORPGs, and TD games[/b] for that matter continuously evolve, we wanted to add something new to the mix.

A fun moment happened a year after release when I was at [b]Slush[/b], showcasing Megapop. One of the [b]leads from the PvZ team[/b] reached out to meet for coffee. He told me he had [b]asked his entire team to play Trolls as an inspiration[/b], since we had solved many mechanics in different ways. That was a cool full-circle moment.

[h2][b]The State of TD Games Today[/b][/h2]

I feel like [b]tower defense as a genre has hit a bit of a wall[/b]. The rise of [b]idle mechanics, free-to-play monetization, and service-game models[/b] has led to a lack of fresh ideas. While there are still great TD games, truly [b]new[/b] experiences seem rare.

That’s why, with [b]Trolls Reborn[/b], we [b]returned to the core[/b]—back to [b]hardcore strategy[/b]. We removed [b]free-to-play restrictions[/b], increased difficulty, and added [b]more active gameplay[/b] where the entire battlefield is an [b]active combat zone[/b].

We hope to keep tinkering and [b]pushing Trolls forward[/b] in the years to come, staying true to this vision of a [b]dynamic, engaging TD experience[/b]. Hopefully enough of you will like the game, and buy the full release, so we can see that become a reality. Still, that remains to be seen, but we shall at least do our very best!

[h2][b]What Do You Think?[/b][/h2]

Do you have comments or want us to cover something specific? Let us know, and we’ll get back to you!

All the best,
[b]Jørgen Tharaldsen[/b]

notes.title: Thanks for playing the Demo!
notes.notes:
Today, we simply wanted to thank everyone who has tried the demo so far! It’s been wonderful for us to get this version of [u]Trolls vs Vikings[/u] out on Steam, and it's great to see so many people enjoying it! We've definitively increased the complexity of the game, as well as how it evolves and looks, so we are grateful that it seems to have resonated well. So far.

We’ve been closely monitoring comments and reactions across the web, responding where possible. Thanks to everyone who has taken the time to share their thoughts. Your feedback is invaluable!

More than anything, we've been on the lookout for bugs or pain points we hadn’t anticipated. Thankfully, the game is more or less as stable as we expected, but a handful of unexpected bugs have been caught—good on you for finding and reporting them! We've fixed all the issues we've encountered over the past few days, and these fixes will be included in the next update.

Our next big milestone is Steam Next Fest, where we’ll have another round of the demo before the full launch on [b]March 7th[/b]!

On a personal note, I was a little anxious about the complexity of [u]Brutal Difficulty[/u]. Would it be too brutal—only enjoyable for us developers? It [b]is[/b] really hard, but we've already seen players who have (almost) completed all the levels. While some levels have been called "impossible," the full game will bring more shards, more power, and additional spells as players progress. If no one can clear every level now, they surely will later on.

Is it too hard? We’ll see. But we wanted it to be a [b]true test[/b].

Nothing is impossible, by the way—we've personally completed all levels on multiple setups. It may push you to the limit, but that’s the point of the challenge. You need to be **active—really active—**on that difficulty level.

We’ll keep sharing updates as we progress toward launch, giving you more insights into the game’s development, our design choices, and everything happening behind the scenes.

Hopefully, you'll continue the journey with us—we can’t wait to fully open the gates soon!

[b]All the best,[/b]
Jørgen Tharaldsen
[b][u]Game Director, Trolls vs Vikings[/u][/b]

notes.title: The Music of Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn
notes.notes:
Alright, folks, talk about something that hits you right in the gut (in a good way!): the sound and music of [i]Trolls Reborn[/i]! From the very beginning, we knew that the music needed to [b]stomp, roar, and shake the very foundations of Viking longhouses![/b]

So, when we started plotting [i]Trolls Reborn[/i], one of the first things we did was reach out to the legendary [b]Aleksandar Dimitrijevic[/b], our original composer who lives close by our office, and ask, [i]“Hey, want to remaster the old tracks?”[/i] And what does he do? He pulls a full-on Troll move and surprises us with, [i]“I got really inspired over the weekend, so I made you a whole new Troll track.”[/i] [u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f92f.png[/img][/u]

Boom! That’s how [i]Trolls Forever[/i] was born. Not only are we bringing back all those glorious tunes, but we’ve also got [b]brand-new music[/b] just for [i]Reborn[/i], as well as adding a whole set of freshly remastered music from Trolls 2. So, new, not new!

[h3][b]Meet the Maestro [/b][b][u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1fa84.png[/img][/u][/b][/h3]

If you don’t know Aleksandar by name, you [b]definitely[/b] know his work. He’s contributed music for [b]Avatar, Star Wars, Lord of The Rings, Marvel, Wall-E, Pirates of The Caribbean, Narnia, Harry Potter, Stranger Things, Terminator, Game of Thrones, X-Files, Simpsons, 1917, Free Solo, Spiderman, Wolverine, Batman, Hunger Games, Jurassic World[/b]… I mean, stringing up all those titles. It’s almost otherworldly!

(Full list? Knock yourself out: [url=https://aleksandardimitrijevic.com/index.php/trailers/]Aleksandar's Trailer Work[/url])

Now, before you start thinking we somehow roped in a Hollywood composer for fun—plot twist! Aleksandar actually doesn’t compose music [b]for[/b] those movies. Nope. He makes [b]the epic trailer music[/b] that gets your blood pumping before the movie even starts. You know that moment when the bass drops in a trailer, and you instantly want to ride into battle and order that movie ticket? Yeah. That’s him. And, he’s bringing that same fire to [i]Trolls Reborn[/i].

[h3][b]Trolls, Gnomes & a Very Real Orchestra [/b][b][u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f3bb.png[/img][/u][/b][/h3]

When we first started working with Aleksandar, we thought, [i]“Hey, what if we didn’t just make a soundtrack? What if we went full madness and hired actual Trolls and Gnomes to play it?”[/i] And, well… that’s [i]kind of[/i] what we did.

We brainstormed what it would actually sound like if a Troll tried to play a human string instrument. (Spoiler: [b]wonky[/b].) So, naturally, we [b]went into the woods[/b] to find the right creatures for the job. And lo and behold—[b]we found real Trolls who wanted in![/b]

Okay, maybe not [i]actual[/i] Trolls, but we had an absolute blast recording with musicians and sound designers who helped craft this otherworldly, stomping, clanging, rumbling [i]Trolls Reborn[/i] soundscape.

[h3][b]When Vikings Show Up, You Better Have Guitars [/b][b][u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f3b8.png[/img][/u][/b][/h3]

[i]Trolls[/i] aren’t just about [b]Trolls[/b]—we’ve also got [b]Vikings and gods[/b] to contend with! So when you’re facing off against Odin or Thor, you better believe the soundtrack is going [b]hard.[/b] We’re talking [b]rolling guitars, booming drums, and that intense “Oh sh*t, I’m fighting a god” kind of music.[/b]

[h3][b]The Original Madness (with a Touch of Chaos)[/b][/h3]

It’s not just Aleksandar, though. Back in the day, our [b]audio director Tord Digranes[/b] and a whole bunch of amazing sound designers, friends, and devs lent their voices, shouts, grunts, and other [i]Trollish[/i] noises to the original game. For [i]Trolls Reborn[/i], we’ve kept a lot of that magic but updated the tech to make sure everything sounds [b]as good as it can.[/b]

I’ll never forget those recording sessions—[b]friends, devs, and actors crammed into a studio, taking turns growling, grunting, and howling into a mic[/b] while trying not to laugh. We went all in to make [i]Trolls[/i] sound like nothing else out there. And honestly? It was just [b]so much fun[/b]. We hope that shines through in the game.

[h3][b]Wanna Hear [/b][b][i]Trolls Forever[/i][/b][b]? [/b][b][u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f3a7.png[/img][/u][/b][/h3]

You don’t have to take my word for it—check out the brand-new [i]Trolls Forever[/i] track for yourself! I uploaded a sample to SoundCloud, so go have a listen:

[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f50a.png[/img][/u] [url=https://on.soundcloud.com/KUK5mAYYoSBXr27j9]Listen Here[/url] [u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f50a.png[/img][/u]

You also find some other Trolls track on that page if you search. Alas; if you search Aleksandars webpage you find a very gifted composer, making music not only for Trolls and Hollywood, but also his very own awesome albums. Do check him out!

Until next time, keep your battle drums pounding and your war horns blaring! [u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/2694-fe0f.png[/img][/u]

All the best,
[b]Jørgen Tharaldsen[/b]
[i]Game Director, Trolls vs Vikings[/i]

notes.title: Minor Tweaks and Massive Changes
notes.notes:
As we gear up for the launch of [b]Trolls vs Vikings Reborn[/b], I wanted to highlight some of the [b]many changes[/b] we’ve made. A lot of thought and work has gone into this game, so let’s dive into some of the updates!

[h3][b]Speed-Up Button – A Game Changer[/b][/h3]
The [b]speed-up button[/b] is a no-brainer for player satisfaction. It [b]doubles the game speed[/b] with a single tap, making it easier to blast through early waves or grind easier levels. We experimented with multi-step speeds, but found a [b]simple on/off toggle[/b] worked best. Cranking up the difficulty on double speed? That’s a challenge in itself.

While this might seem like an easy feature to add, the original code structure made it surprisingly [b]complex[/b]. Many of the [b]UI elements, animations, and spawn rates[/b] were tied to specific game beats, meaning we had to do some heavy restructuring. [b]Fingar[/b], our coding wizard, initially hit a wall and summed it up perfectly: [i]“uff, that is much harder than it sounds.”[/i] But after some deep diving into the codebase, he cracked the problem.

Personally, I mostly use the speed-up button for [b]early-game setups[/b]—establishing my economy and defenses—or in moments where I know I’ll win and just want to move on. [b](Side note: I’ve tried beating every level on double speed as a personal challenge, but some of the Brutal levels are still getting the better of me. One day!)[/b]

[h3][b]Buster – From Walking to Jumping[/b][/h3]
Let’s talk about [b]Buster[/b], leader of the [b]Troll Liberation Front[/b]. In the original game, he walked from tile to tile. That was a cool mechanic—[b]a movable troll unit in a tower defense game was pretty unique[/b]. But over time, I felt like he was [b]a bit slow and clunky[/b].

For [b]Reborn[/b], we changed his animations, adjusted his design, and most importantly—[b]made him jump instead of walk[/b]. This alone [b]massively improves his responsiveness and battlefield mobility[/b]. But, of course, implementing it wasn’t that simple. Since [b]Trolls vs Vikings[/b] is [b]precise about damage calculations[/b] (when attacks hit, where they land, and how units interact), we had to solve a ton of edge cases. For example: [i]What happens if a Viking swings at Buster, but he jumps away at the last second? Should that count as a hit or a near miss?[/i] We ultimately decided that his [b]damage and HP stay the same[/b], but his improved movement makes him [b]a stronger tactical unit[/b], especially in the [b]early game[/b].

[previewyoutube=mLkRhl0X-4w;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Buster – A Trickster’s Best Friend[/b][/h3]
One thing we realized with Buster’s new jumping ability is that he can be used to [b]bait and manipulate enemy behavior[/b]. This is where things get really fun.
For example, the [b]Archer Vikings[/b], one of the [b]nastiest enemies[/b] in the game, are lethal from a distance. But—if Buster jumps right in front of them, they instantly swap to melee combat instead. No arrows to dodge, no relentless ranged pressure. Just a good old-fashioned brawl where Buster actually stands a chance.

And then there’s the [b]Stilt Vikings[/b]—those guys who tower over the battlefield, making them a real pain to deal with. With his jump, Buster can [b]force them to stumble and fall off their stilts[/b]. Watching a Stilt Viking go from towering menace to scrambling on the ground? [i]Chef’s kiss.[/i]

[h3][b]Tactical Depth – Buster & The Dwarf Duo[/b][/h3]
I’ve added a short [b]video clip[/b] from one of our new [b]special missions[/b], where [b]Buster and the Dwarf[/b] work together. [b]Buster acts as a frontline tank (since he can heal), while the Dwarf deals heavy damage from behind.[/b] The Dwarf’s [b]chain attack[/b] has just enough range to stay out of reach of enemy spears, and—[b]pro tip[/b]—the closer he is, the faster he attacks since the chain has less distance to travel.

This setup creates a [b]powerful but high-maintenance duo[/b]. Moving them dynamically across the board makes them lethal, but it also demands [b]constant attention[/b]. If you like an [b]active, strategic playstyle[/b], this is for you!

[h3][b]The Chess Connection[/b][/h3]
I’m a [b]hardcore chess player[/b]. I’ve played daily since I was six, competed at some point, and even worked on a [b]chess game at Funcom[/b]. That mindset bleeds into [b]Trolls vs Vikings[/b]—the board is [b]an active battlefield, not a static defense line[/b].

Buster, in particular, [b]plays like a Knight or a Bishop[/b]—quick, dynamic, and capable of changing the game if used correctly. But like in chess, a [b]misplayed piece can become dead weight[/b]. If you throw Buster into the wrong fight, he’ll get crushed. If you [b]position him smartly[/b], he can [b]swing an entire battle in your favor[/b].
[b]Reading the Battlefield – The Damage Face[/b]

[b]Trolls vs Vikings[/b] is often [b]pure chaos[/b], with battles raging across the board. That’s why [b]Mikael Noguchi[/b], our [b]art director[/b], put extra effort into [b]facial expressions[/b]. [b]When Buster starts looking beat up, that’s your cue to pull him back and let him recover—if you can![/b]That’s all for this update!

What do you think? Is there anything you’d like to hear more about in future updates? Drop a comment, and we’ll try to cover it!

[b]All the best,[/b]

Jørgen Tharaldsen
[b]Game Director[/b]
[b]Trolls vs Vikings Reborn[/b]

notes.title: Welcome to Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn!
notes.notes:
First off, we [b]hope you’ll love this game[/b] as much as we loved making it! Trolls vs Vikings was born from our [b]passion for tower defense games[/b] (yes, including a certain plant-based classic). I, as Game Director, played every tower defense game I could get my hands on—until finally the idea came. [b]What if we made our own, infused with Norwegian mythology?[/b]

And so, [b]Trolls vs Vikings was born![/b] Unlike most lore, we made [b]the Trolls the good guys[/b], defending their homeland against a [b]Viking invasion[/b].

[img]https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2940040/extras/Trolls_VS_Vikings_Reborn_Steam_Revitalizing_Art.gif?t=1738073369[/img]

The game [b]originally launched on mobile[/b], but that was mainly because it was the go-to platform at the time. Soon after, we brought it to [b]Windows PC via the Windows Store[/b], and despite my initial doubts about mouse (and partly) keyboard controls, the [b]player response was overwhelmingly positive[/b]. [b]1.3 million players later,[/b] we know that many of you had a great time with Trolls.

But even as the years passed, [b]the Trolls legacy never faded[/b]. [b]New players kept discovering it[/b], despite no major updates. Still, I always felt there was [b]so much more we could have done[/b]—and, more strongly, that [b]the free-to-play model held the game back.[/b]

[h2][u][b]A True Premium Tower Defense Experience[/b][/u][/h2]

As a developer, I’ve seen how [b]free-to-play models often dilute great gameplay[/b]—designed more for monetization than pure fun. I get why it happens, but this time, with [b]Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/b], we’ve had the absolute [b]freedom to focus entirely on player satisfaction[/b]. Just [b]pure, strategic, moment-to-moment gameplay[/b].

Early in 2024, the opportunity to return to Trolls finally came. While [b]most of the original team had moved on[/b], I was able to put together [b]a small but dedicated crew [/b]to rebuild it with me.

Our goal was clear:

[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/2714-fe0f.png[/img][/u] [b]Make the game even more gameplay-focused[/b]
[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/2714-fe0f.png[/img][/u] [b]Add brutal new difficulties and missions[/b]
[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/2714-fe0f.png[/img][/u] [b]Remove all the free-to-play clutter[/b]
[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/2714-fe0f.png[/img][/u] [b]Revamp the upgrade, spell, and evolution systems[/b]
[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/2714-fe0f.png[/img][/u] Upgrade all the graphics, make all new Vikings and improve animations

I wanted to create [b]something I’d love playing myself[/b]—a game that delivers the [b]intensity and challenge that modern tower defenses often lack[/b]. That sounds quite narcissistic, but sometimes as a developer you are your own best target audience.

[img]https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2940040/extras/Trolls_VS_Vikings_Reborn_Steam_Pure_Gameplay_Experience_1.gif?t=1738073369[/img]

[h2][u][b]What’s New in Reborn?[/b][/u][/h2]

If you played the original, you’ll recognize [b]many of the characters and story elements[/b]—but we’ve made some [b]huge improvements[/b]:
[list]
[*] [b]New music & sound design
[*] Revamped art & all-new Viking models/animations
[*] Brutal difficulty modefor hardcore strategists
[*] Overhauled UI, spell system, and core mechanics
[*] Speed-up button for faster-paced action
[*] More moment-to-moment tactical decisions[/b]
[/list]

That last part is important—[b]this version is built for a dedicated Steam audience[/b].

The [b]Brutal mode[/b] in particular is no joke. I’m sure [b]most players will struggle to beat all the levels[/b], but that’s the point! It’s designed to push you to [b]experiment with strategy, spells, and upgrades[/b]—to give that [b]“just one more try” feeling[/b] that makes great strategy games so addicting.

(And yes, I personally tested them all over and over and over in multiple configurations. They are tough, but [b]100% beatable.[/b] [u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f608.png[/img][/u])

[h2][u][b]We Want to Hear From You![/b][/u][/h2]

That’s enough words for today, but we’ll be back with more posts as we get closer to [b]launch on March 7th[/b]!

In the meantime—[b]we’d love to hear from you![/b]
[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f4ac.png[/img][/u] [b]Have you tried the demo?[/b] What’s your favorite part so far?
[u][img]https://a.slack-edge.com/production-standard-emoji-assets/14.0/google-medium/1f4a1.png[/img][/u] [b]Got feedback?[/b] Let us know in the comments!

See you in battle!

[b]Jørgen Tharaldsen[/b]
Game Director, [b]Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn[/b]

notes.title: Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn demo is live and is Trolls-tastic!
notes.notes:
After a decade, the wait is over! The tower defence behemoth Trolls vs Vikings is finally back, and better than ever!

Trolls vs Vikings: Reborn is a completely revamped premium edition of the legendary tower defence showdown. And guess what? You don’t have to wait until launch day on March 7th to dive in—the Steam Demo is available right now from January 28 to February 3.

This isn’t just a trip down memory lane—it’s a full-blown Nordic brawl with tons of new content, slick new visuals and music, and enough gameplay additions to make even Odin raise an eyebrow. Even more, it’s optimized for the Steam PC platform, which marks a first for the series. 

Whether you’re a die-hard fan of the original (over 1.3 million of you!) or a newcomer to the chaos, you’re in for a troll-sized treat!

[previewyoutube=ZrcStvuHzTg;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]“I’m a huge fan of tower defense games, but it’s getting truly hard to find ones that aren’t bogged down in free-to-play traps or idling too far into casual gameplay,”[/i] says Game Director Jørgen Tharaldsen. [i]“With Reborn, we’re bringing the focus back to the core strategy and tower defense enthusiasts—those of us who love games packed with options and tactical depth where every choice counts and every second matters.”[/i]
